sourceFile: "intercessory_25-26_4-14-2026.pdf", provided directly by Josh via Google Drive (file id 11SpVIKTeODLXHI5h6O4WB0fd9epvMZ6-, folder "TEC Cycle of Prayer")
notes: The source's own cycle runs Advent 2025 (Sunday, November 30, 2025) through Christ the King Sunday (Sunday, November 22, 2026), keyed to lectionary Sunday names with explicit calendar dates printed alongside each one. Only the portion landing in calendar year 2026 (January 4, 2026 through November 22, 2026, inclusive -- 47 Sundays) is included here; the four Advent-through-Christmas 2025 Sundays are out of this file's calendar-year scope and not included.

Two appendix sections in the source are not part of the weekly Sunday cycle and are excluded from `entries` entirely: a 'Clergy Spouses and Surviving Clergy Spouses' name roster (embedded under March 8's entry, whose category subject IS retained) and an 'ANNIVERSARIES' section (ordination/consecration anniversary dates for clergy, organized by month, unrelated to the per-Sunday rotation). Both sections' internal column layout was also garbled in this file's text extraction and could not be reliably re-ordered.
The August 9 entry's 'Non-Parochial, Non-Stipendiary, Non-Resident Licensed, Resident/Non-Geographical and Retired Clergy' category likewise omits the source's attached name list.

Several category subjects (Christ Church Cathedral, July 12; St. Augustine's Chapel/Campus Ministry, August 16) have their city inferred or omitted per this corpus's rule against fabricating an unstated place -- disclosed on each such subject's own `note` field. 'St. Philip's Episcopal Church' (April 19) is recorded as a `category` rather than `parish` for the same reason: no city was given.

January 4's 'Emmanuel Episcopal Church' place ('Winchester') is inferred from this same source's own later, more complete listing of the identical parish name on November 15, 2026; the city is not repeated in the January 4 line itself.
'St. Andrew's Episcopal Church, Lexintgon' (September 6) preserves the source's own apparent typo for 'Lexington' verbatim, per this corpus's standing rule against silently correcting spelling.

Each parish/category subject's `note` field holds the specific clergy/warden name(s) and title(s) the source prints alongside that entry that week -- the source's own per-week content, not an editorial annotation.
